Station 01 of 06

Exterior & grade

Not seen

We walk the perimeter first: where soil meets siding, where downspouts dump, where mulch is banked against the foundation. The flashlight finds what a glance misses.

Checked · grade slope · mulch depth · wood-to-soil · vent screens · downspouts

Termites or flying ants?

Found wings on a windowsill? Tap what the bug looked like.

Waist
Wings
Antennae

Straight waist, equal wings and straight antennae point to termite swarmers. Bag a few and keep them for us.

Book an inspection

Why a raised house

Most houses here sit over a crawlspace. Damp sand, warm air, wood a foot off the ground: that is where we spend the most time.

02

Station 02 of 06

Mud tubes & crawlspace

Conducive

Mud tubes are the pencil-wide tunnels termites build from soil to wood. We break one open to see if it is active, then probe the wood behind it. Under the house we look for standing water, wood touching soil and blocked vents.

Checked · block piers · vapor barrier · standing water · vent flow

Does your crawlspace invite termites?

Open the hatch with a flashlight. Tick what you see.

Each tick is a condition we would mark Conducive.

Book an inspection

Stations 03 & 04 of 06

Inside the wood, then up top

03Seen

Foundation wood & band board

The wood sitting on the foundation is the first wood termites reach from the soil. We tap and probe it end to end. Hollow sound or a soft spot gets photographed and written up.

04Not seen

Attic & under the sinks

Roof leaks and slow drips feed termites too. We check the attic sheathing, pipe collars and the cabinets under every sink for damp wood and droppings.

05

Station 05 of 06

Perimeter & yard: what we treat

Every visit starts with the same walk-around. What we find decides which of these you need, and which you do not.
